_comment: Merge into your Claude Code settings.json (user-level %USERPROFILE%/.claude/settings.json or project .claude/settings.json). This uses the EXEC form ('command' = the interpreter, 'args' = its arguments): Claude Code spawns it directly with NO shell, so the script path in args is passed literally (no backslash-escaping and no quoting), even under 'Program Files' or on Windows. Set 'command' to the Python that should run the script: 'python3' on most macOS/Linux (a bare 'python' often does not exist there), 'python' on Windows, or -- most robust on any OS -- the absolute interpreter path from `python -c "import sys; print(sys.executable)"`. Replace the args path with the absolute path to engramory_index_guard.py. Optional, and usually unnecessary: ENGRAMORY_INDEX_IGNORE exempts a MEMORY.md that is NOT a real index -- a comma-separated list of absolute paths or bare basenames. A full path exempts only that one file; a bare basename exempts every file with that name, INCLUDING both real indexes, so use it sparingly. In the standard two-tier setup you need neither: the filename default guards memory/MEMORY.md and ~/.engramory/MEMORY.md and nothing else. See the env var table in hooks/INSTALL.md.
